name: Support SLA Engine (business-hours clocks, pause/resume, escalation, daily report)

parameters.content:
## Support SLA Engine
Tracks first-response and resolution SLAs in **business time** (time zone, working hours, weekends and holidays), with pause while waiting for the customer, and escalates automatically.

**Events in:** `POST /webhook/sla-event` (Header Auth) with `{type, external_id, ...}`:
`created` (subject, customer, priority, assignee), `first_response`, `pause`, `resume`, `resolve`. Call it from your helpdesk, a form or another workflow.
**Every 5 minutes:** scans open tickets and alerts **once** per ticket and clock when 80 % of the target is used (at risk) and when it is breached.
**Daily 09:00:** compliance report per priority.

**Before running:** run `sql/schema.sql`, set your calendar and holidays (`sql/example_setup.sql`), create credentials (Postgres, Telegram, Header Auth 'SLA webhook key'), replace `REPLACE_WITH_SUPPORT_CHAT_ID` and `REPLACE_ID`, set the Error Workflow to this workflow.

### Clock rules
- Open: both clocks run. Pause (waiting on customer): clocks stop, remaining business minutes are saved. Resume: due times are recomputed from now.
- First response needs an open ticket. Resolving a ticket with no response counts the resolution as the first response.
- Every change uses optimistic locking (`version`). A concurrent change answers `409`: just retry.
- `urgent` uses a 24x7 calendar by default; every other priority uses business time.

parameters.query:
SELECT p.priority, p.first_response_min, p.resolution_min, p.calendar,
       c.timezone, c.work_days, c.start_minute, c.end_minute,
       COALESCE((SELECT array_agg(to_char(h.day, 'YYYY-MM-DD')) FROM holidays h
                 WHERE h.day BETWEEN current_date - 7 AND current_date + 400), ARRAY[]::text[]) AS holidays
FROM sla_policies p CROSS JOIN business_calendar c
WHERE p.priority = $1::text;

INSERT INTO tickets (external_id, subject, customer, priority, assignee, response_due_at, resolution_due_at)
VALUES ($1::text, $2::text, NULLIF($3::text, ''), $4::text, NULLIF($5::text, ''), $6::timestamptz, $7::timestamptz)
ON CONFLICT (external_id) DO NOTHING
RETURNING id, external_id, priority, status, response_due_at, resolution_due_at;

parameters.responseBody: ={{ $json.id ? { status: 'created', ticket: $json.external_id, priority: $json.priority, response_due_at: $json.response_due_at, resolution_due_at: $json.resolution_due_at } : { status: 'duplicate', message: 'Ticket already exists' } }}

parameters.query:
UPDATE tickets SET
  status = $3::text,
  first_response_at = NULLIF($4::text, '')::timestamptz,
  response_met = NULLIF($5::text, '')::boolean,
  resolved_at = NULLIF($6::text, '')::timestamptz,
  resolution_met = NULLIF($7::text, '')::boolean,
  response_remaining_min = NULLIF($8::text, '')::numeric,
  resolution_remaining_min = NULLIF($9::text, '')::numeric,
  response_due_at = NULLIF($10::text, '')::timestamptz,
  resolution_due_at = NULLIF($11::text, '')::timestamptz,
  version = version + 1,
  updated_at = now()
WHERE external_id = $1::text AND version = $2::int
RETURNING id, external_id, status, version, first_response_at, response_met, resolved_at, resolution_met, response_due_at, resolution_due_at;

parameters.responseBody: ={{ $json.id ? { status: 'ok', ticket: $json.external_id, state: $json.status, response_due_at: $json.response_due_at, resolution_due_at: $json.resolution_due_at, response_met: $json.response_met, resolution_met: $json.resolution_met } : { status: 'conflict', error: 'The ticket changed at the same time. Retry the request.' } }}

parameters.query:
SELECT c.timezone, c.work_days, c.start_minute, c.end_minute,
       COALESCE((SELECT array_agg(to_char(h.day, 'YYYY-MM-DD')) FROM holidays h
                 WHERE h.day BETWEEN current_date - 7 AND current_date + 400), ARRAY[]::text[]) AS holidays
FROM business_calendar c;

SELECT t.id, t.external_id, t.subject, t.customer, t.priority, t.assignee, t.first_response_at,
       t.response_due_at, t.resolution_due_at, t.response_alert_level, t.resolution_alert_level,
       p.first_response_min, p.resolution_min, p.calendar
FROM tickets t JOIN sla_policies p ON p.priority = t.priority
WHERE t.status = 'open'
  AND ((t.first_response_at IS NULL AND t.response_alert_level < 2) OR t.resolution_alert_level < 2)
ORDER BY LEAST(t.response_due_at, t.resolution_due_at)
LIMIT 500;

UPDATE tickets SET
  response_alert_level = CASE WHEN $2::text = 'response' THEN GREATEST(response_alert_level, $3::int) ELSE response_alert_level END,
  resolution_alert_level = CASE WHEN $2::text = 'resolution' THEN GREATEST(resolution_alert_level, $3::int) ELSE resolution_alert_level END
WHERE id = $1::bigint AND status = 'open'
  AND (($2::text = 'response' AND response_alert_level < $3::int) OR ($2::text = 'resolution' AND resolution_alert_level < $3::int))
RETURNING id, external_id, subject, customer, priority, assignee, $2::text AS clock, $3::int AS level;

SELECT p.priority,
  COUNT(t.id) FILTER (WHERE t.status = 'open')::int AS open,
  COUNT(t.id) FILTER (WHERE t.status = 'pending')::int AS pending,
  COUNT(t.id) FILTER (WHERE t.status = 'open' AND (t.response_alert_level = 2 OR t.resolution_alert_level = 2))::int AS breached_open,
  COUNT(t.id) FILTER (WHERE t.resolved_at > now() - interval '24 hours')::int AS resolved_24h,
  COUNT(t.id) FILTER (WHERE t.resolved_at > now() - interval '24 hours' AND t.resolution_met)::int AS resolution_met_24h,
  COUNT(t.id) FILTER (WHERE t.first_response_at > now() - interval '24 hours')::int AS responded_24h,
  COUNT(t.id) FILTER (WHERE t.first_response_at > now() - interval '24 hours' AND t.response_met)::int AS response_met_24h,
  ROUND((AVG(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (t.first_response_at - t.created_at)) / 60)
         FILTER (WHERE t.first_response_at > now() - interval '24 hours'))::numeric, 0) AS avg_first_response_min
FROM sla_policies p LEFT JOIN tickets t ON t.priority = p.priority
GROUP BY p.priority, p.first_response_min
ORDER BY p.first_response_min;
